note: Derived from the 8/19 read-only audit, reconciled against the in-house 8/13 cleanup review and a second review on 8/20. The test for a negative here is NOT cost-per-conversion -- it is whether the term can produce an admission. Several blocked terms have converted cheaply, and that is the point: a detox or inpatient seeker who fills in a form is a referred-out on the admission board, not revenue. Competitor and partner terms are the opposite case -- service-appropriate for what OCH actually delivers -- which is why they are protected rather than blocked.

heldPendingClientAnswer.note: Proposed as negatives but deliberately NOT applied until JB answers. Each would be wrong to block if the answer comes back yes.
keywords: virtual — does OCH run a telehealth IOP? Also decides whether Dayton and Columbus are servable without a building.
medicare — the largest single referred-out disqualifier in the fit analysis, but blocking it presumes OCH does not accept Medicare. Needs confirming, not assuming.

budgets.reason: EXCEPTION to the standing no-increases-until-results rule, taken deliberately and before 8/25. Branded converts at $22-32 CPA, the cheapest in the account, and the keyword that made it look expensive ('ohiorecoverycenters' phrase, $559 for 2 conversions) was removed on 8/13. Note the tension: the raise was decided on the 30-day budget-lost figure of 70.3%, and the 7-day figure is 23.7% -- most of that headroom had already closed by the time the change was made. Treat this as a test, not a settled case. If impression share does not move within a week, the remaining constraint is Ad Rank (45.7% on 7 days) and the fix is ad relevance and the landing page, not money.

campaignNegatives.reason: Levels of care OCH cannot admit for. Already present on Branded; TCS was never covered. Three of these have converted historically -- 'midwest detox' ($7.73, 1 conv), 'inpatient substance abuse treatment near me' ($8.77, 1 conv), 'ucpc methadone clinic' ($10.62, 1 conv) -- roughly a $9 CPA. They are blocked anyway because a form fill from someone OCH must refer out is a cost, not a conversion. This is the same admissibility test that protects the competitor and CCAT clusters, applied in the other direction.

knownRedundancies: 'methadone clinic' is fully covered by phrase 'methadone'; kept only because it is already live and removing it is a separate mutate type this tool does not support.
'residential treatment' is fully covered by phrase 'residential', added 8/20 after the narrower form was found not to catch 'residential drug treatment programs near me', which served last month.
'detoxification' is NOT redundant with 'detox' -- phrase match works on word sequences, not substrings.
